name: Warm American narrator (40s)
summary: Warm, grounded middle-low baritone; calm, precise and unhurried.
description: A male audiobook narrator around forty years old, speaking clear, natural American English. A warm, grounded middle-low register with a mature, lightly textured timbre. Slightly sober and reflective, with balanced, restrained expressiveness and natural sentence melody. The voice feels human and engaged rather than theatrical or flat.

text: The evening light fell across the quiet garden, and for a while nothing moved. He waited by the gate, listening for footsteps on the other side. When they came at last, they were slower than he remembered, and he understood, before the latch lifted, that the news would not be good.

text: The library opened a little after sunrise. A narrow beam of light crossed the floor, touching the row of books beside the window. For a moment, the room seemed exactly as it had the night before. Then she noticed the envelope waiting on the empty desk.

name: Dry, understated young man (mid-20s)
summary: Grounded baritone; states absurd things completely straight.
description: A young man of twenty-five with a grounded baritone, slightly rough at the edges, with a plain working-class American delivery. Dry and understated, he states absurd things with complete seriousness. Quietly warm with friends, flat and guarded with anyone he doesn't trust. Delivery: Never sell the joke; deliver the disaster like a minor technical fault. Under threat, drop the play entirely and go low and exact.
reference_description: A young man around twenty-five with a calm, clear light-baritone voice and natural American English. Measured and thoughtful, quietly warm, never theatrical.
text: I know what it looks like. But I've been over it twice, and the numbers don't change. If we go now, we're there before the light goes. If we wait, we're only guessing, and I'm tired of guessing.

name: Gravelly, deadpan man (late 20s)
summary: Warm, gravelly baritone; big exaggerations told with total sincerity.
description: A big man in his late twenties with a warm, slightly gravelly baritone and an easygoing blue-collar American delivery. He builds absurd exaggerations with total sincerity and visible enjoyment. When things turn dangerous, he becomes short, firm and protective. Delivery: Play every exaggeration as if it were sober logistics; the comedy is in his seriousness. Snap to clipped commands the moment someone is at risk.
reference_description: A man in his late twenties with a deep, dry, slightly gravelly baritone and relaxed American English. Deadpan and matter-of-fact; says absurd things completely straight, without signalling the joke.
text: Right. So the plan is we drive four hours north, in the snow, with two dogs and a heater that only works when it feels like it, because a man in a grey coat said so. Brilliant. I'll pack the sandwiches.

name: Precise, quietly ironic woman (mid-20s)
summary: Bright, clear mezzo; polite questions that do the teasing.
description: A woman in her mid-twenties with a bright, clear mezzo and precise, educated American diction. Polite, attentive and quietly amused, she lets careful questions do the teasing. Under pressure she turns formal and steady, her emotion audible only in her breathing. Delivery: Keep the politeness genuine and the amusement in the last word. When frightened, organize the words, don't raise them.
reference_description: A woman in her mid-twenties with a clear, bright mezzo-soprano voice and crisp, articulate American English. Precise and polite, with dry, understated irony.
text: Let me make sure I understand. You signed it, you didn't read it, and now you'd like me to find the clause that says you never signed it. That's very kind of you. I'll start with page one.

name: Husky, blunt young woman (early 20s)
summary: Low, slightly husky alto; short lines that end the conversation.
description: A young woman of twenty-three with a low, slightly husky alto and a clipped, streetwise American delivery. Economical and blunt, she ends conversations in a single flat line. Her warmth shows only in brief, unguarded moments. Delivery: Wait, then hit once; never pad the line. In danger she gets lower and more exact, not louder.
reference_description: A young woman in her early twenties with a low, slightly husky alto voice and clear American English. Direct and economical, dry wit, short clipped phrasing, unimpressed but not cold.
text: I told you it would be cold up there. Nobody listens to me until it's too late, and then everyone wants to know why I didn't say anything. I did. Twice.

name: Smooth, courteous, guarded man (late 20s)
summary: Soft, velvety baritone; calm warmth that never raises its voice.
description: A man in his late twenties with a soft, velvety mid-range baritone and careful, cultivated American diction. Calm, attentive and genuinely warm, he makes every listener feel singled out, and the warmth may or may not be sincere. He never raises his voice. Delivery: Play him as kind; let the listener find the control on their own. The quieter the moment, the slower he speaks.
reference_description: A man in his late twenties with a smooth, polished light-tenor voice and precise, educated American English. Composed, courteous and guarded, with even, controlled phrasing.
text: It isn't that I don't trust you. I simply prefer to know where the door is before I walk into the room. Humour me. Tell me again who else knows we're coming, and how they found out.

name: Soft, shy woman with gentle humor (late 20s)
summary: Slightly breathy, shy at first; steady on facts, laughs at her own jokes.
description: A woman in her late twenties with a soft, slightly breathy small-town northern American voice, shy at first and steady when she talks about facts. She tells terrible gentle jokes with a straight face, then laughs at them herself through her nose. Delivery: Let the shyness show in the openings, never in the facts. The laugh after her own joke should sound surprised, not performed.

text: The river went up three centimetres this morning, which is the most exciting thing it's done all week. I wrote it down twice in case it gets ideas. People ask me if measuring water is lonely. I tell them no, it's very fluid. Sorry. That one was bad.

name: Hoarse, gloomy drawl (man, mid-20s)
summary: Lazy, slightly hoarse drawl; dark jokes delivered like weather reports.
description: A man in his mid-twenties with a lazy, slightly hoarse northern rural American drawl and a gloomy, sarcastic edge. Unbothered and dry, he delivers jokes about bad luck and death like weather reports. Never sloppy, never slurred. Delivery: Throw the dark punchline away instead of landing it. When something real happens, let the drawl vanish and the voice turn suddenly sober.
